Reduce values by group

Source: R/grp-reduce.R
grp_reduce.Rd

grp_reduce() computes a statistic of x for each group of by, in one pass over the rows. With several columns in x, each with its own fn, all of them are reduced in that one pass, and the rows are grouped once.

Usage

grp_reduce(x, by, fn = "sum", na.rm = TRUE, broadcast = "none")

Arguments

x

A vector, or a list or data frame of vectors as long as the keys; a list is several columns, so a list column goes inside one. count, nobs, first and last take any vector; min and max also integer, double, logical, character, Date and POSIXct ones; sum, prod and mean take numbers and logicals.

by

The result of grp(), or key vectors for grp() to group by: a vector, or a data frame or list of them.

fn

The statistic: "sum", "prod", "mean", "min", "max", "count", "nobs", "first" or "last"; one, or one per column of x.

na.rm

Leave missing values out.

broadcast

"none" for one value per group, in the order of grp()'s identifiers, so that it lines up with keys; or one value per row: "replace", each row's group value, "subtract", x less it, or "divide", x over it. A character or factor x takes "none" and "replace" only.

Value

A vector when x is one vector, else a list with one per column. When by is key vectors, the grp() result is attached as the attribute "groups", so that its keys and sizes need no second grouping.

Details

The statistics follow base R: sum, prod and mean are base sum(), prod() and mean() over each group's values, bit for bit, and return double, for integer x too. min and max keep x's type and class; character values compare by their bytes in UTF-8, not by locale. count is the group's size, nobs its values that are not missing, and first and last its first and last value.

With na.rm = TRUE, the default, missing values (NA, and NaN for doubles, as is.na() has them) are left out; a group with no other value gives NA for sum, prod, mean, min and max, where base sum() would give 0 and min() Inf. With na.rm = FALSE a missing value makes the group's statistic missing, as in base R, and first and last return the value in place.

Examples

g <- grp(c("a", "b", "a", "b"))
grp_reduce(c(1, 2, 3, NA), g, "sum")
#> [1] 4 2
grp_reduce(c(1, 2, 3, NA), g, "sum", na.rm = FALSE)
#> [1]  4 NA
grp_reduce(list(v = c(1, 2, 3, 4), w = 4:1), g, c("mean", "max"))
#> $v
#> [1] 2 3
#> 
#> $w
#> [1] 4 3
#> 
grp_reduce(c(1, 2, 3, 4), g, "mean", broadcast = "subtract")
#> [1] -1 -1  1  1
s <- grp_reduce(c(5, 1, 2), c("x", "y", "x"), "sum")
attr(s, "groups")$keys
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "x" "y"
#>
